subject: Question concerning testing directional hypothesis with an interaction

messages.author: a0f5c47e0d2e4773
messages.subject: Question concerning testing directional hypothesis with an interaction
parts:
I have teens and adults in my data set, and wish to test a hypothesis that the influence of a brain region  on a personality trait is greater in teens than it is in adults. The adults are the dummy factor.


Does it make sense to compare the coefficient of the interaction to the main effect directly? (A)  Or should I account for the intercept and main effect of age? (B)

(A) hypothesis(MODEL, "AGE_GROUPTEEN:node_275  > node_275", alpha = .10)

(B) hypothesis(MODEL, "AGE_GROUPTEEN:node_275 + AGE_GROUPTEEN + Intercept  > node_275 + Intercept", alpha = .10)

I am thinking probably A, but interactions can be a little tricky to think about.

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] Question concerning testing directional hypothesis with an interaction
parts:
Assuming AGE_GROUP and node to be dummy coded, the estimate of teens at node 275 is

"AGE_GROUPTEEN:node_275 + AGE_GROUPTEEN + node_275 + Intercept"

while the estimate of adults at node 275 is

"node_275 + Intercept"

Hence we have

hypothesis(MODEL, "AGE_GROUPTEEN:node_275 + AGE_GROUPTEEN + node_275 + Intercept > node_275 + Intercept", alpha = .10)

or after simplifying:

hypothesis(MODEL, "AGE_GROUPTEEN:node_275 + AGE_GROUPTEEN  > 0", alpha = .10)
